proof:
One has $a-h=(2-h)(h+1)/[3(h-1)]>0$. The truncated trapezoid $D$ has centroid zero by reflection in $y$ and
$$
\int_{-h}^{1}2x(a+x)\,dx=2(1+h^3)/3+a(1-h^2)=0.
$$
Integrating $2(a+x)$ gives $|D|=(a+1)^2-(a-h)^2$. Since $B$ lies in $x\le1<h$, the base projection of either oblique section of the prism is exactly $D$. The graph area has the constant Jacobian $\sqrt{1+1/h^2}$, so its centroid is the graph point over the centroid of $D$, namely zero. In either oriented cap, the captured vertical length over $D$ is $1-x/h$, whose integral is $|D|$. Over $B\setminus D$ the captured length is $2$ since $x<-h$. Dividing by the prism volume $2|B|$ gives the displayed $p$. For either inward raw normal $(-1/h,0,\pm1)$, the section area divided by its normal norm is $|D|$. The prism centroid is $(g_B,0)$, giving the displayed $s$ by coarea. Complementation reverses the scalar and gives volume fraction $1-p$.

For a vertical plane above the line through the centered chord $[-q,q]$, its section is $[-q,q]\times[-1,1]$, with centroid zero, and its cap fractions are exactly the planar fractions. A rotation $R$ by $90$ degrees gives a raw planar normal $Rq$ of norm $\lVert q\rVert$ and section length $2\lVert q\rVert$. The normalized coarea vector for the prism is $(2Rq/|B|,0)$, giving the same scalar as for the planar section. At a transverse edge intersection of $B$ and $-B$, the rational linear equations give a rational point $q$ with $q,-q\in\partial B$. Since $0$ is interior, they are the endpoints of the full centered chord. For example an exterior point $(-\ell,b)$ with rational parameters $h<\ell<a$, $|b|<a-\ell$ can be added by convex hull to produce a polygon with extra vertices. No symmetry of the full prism about the oblique planes is needed.
statement:
For rational $1<h<2$ set $a=2(h^2-h+1)/(3(h-1))$, $W=\{(x,y):x\le1,\ |y|\le a+x\}$ and $D=W\cap\{x\ge-h\}$. For a rational convex polygon $B$ with $D\subseteq B\subseteq W$ and any additional vertices at $x<-h$, let $K=B\times[-1,1]$. Its planes $z=\pm x/h$ cut sections with centroid zero. Let $p$ be the inward cap fraction and $s=S(u\cdot g_K)/|K|$ for inward unit normal $u$ and section area $S$. In both orientations $\pm z\ge x/h$,
$$
p=1-|D|/(2|B|),\qquad s=-|D|(g_B)_x/(2h|B|),\qquad |D|=(a+1)^2-(a-h)^2 .
$$
Complements have data $(1-p,-s)$. A vertical plane over a centered chord $[-q,q]$ has centroidal section and the corresponding planar $p,s$ for $B$, with normalized coarea vector $(2Rq/|B|,0)$ for a right-angle planar rotation $R$. Transverse intersections of edges of $B$ and $-B$ give rational endpoints of centered chords.
title: Rational prisms with two oblique centroidal sections
